question: Should exact requester consumption count as terminal descendant delivery proof even if the requester's later outward send fails?
rationale: That choice determines whether the descendant may stop retrying once its output is incorporated into the requester result; source inspection cannot establish the intended product delivery contract.

options.title: Accept consumption as delivery
options.body: Treat exact, session-scoped requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery evidence, after adding restart proof and narrowing the branch.

options.title: Require outward delivery
options.body: Credit the descendant only after the composed requester result is successfully delivered outward, preserving retries when that send fails.

options.title: Use durable inbox semantics
options.body: Pause this patch and resolve consumed-versus-delivered accounting as part of the broader durable completion inbox design.

recommendation.title: Accept consumption as delivery
recommendation.body: Treat exact, session-scoped requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery evidence, after adding restart proof and narrowing the branch.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent provenance ties them to the cron fallback and persisted subagent delivery surfaces where this semantic boundary is enforced.
